answer: Each identity posts an 80-credit bond and registers one mesa basalt crystal, serial-marked. It must complete three stages: quarry the crystal, cut one facet, and deliver it to a mesa depot, each signed by a different auditor against the serial. A skipped or out-of-order stage, or a reused serial, burns the bond. First fees total 36 credits; the kth identity pays 36+6(k-1), the 1000th 6030, so 1000 fakes cost 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented mesa basalt crystal ring fails: its stage signatures already belong to another identity. An honest holder pays 36 once, then redeems the bond.
